interpretation: A large circle is drawn as a yellow band that encloses and contains eight interlaced arcs. The arcs are each two-banded and coloured yellow, red-brown or green. They overlap one another in a ring around an empty centre. The most likely reading is a schematic of cyclical interconnection: the mutual linking or concatenation of the elements and their qualities, or of the seasons and ages within one cosmic or temporal whole. The outer circle stands for the world or the year, and the interlocking arcs for linked, recurring parts. The empty centre may mark the pivot of the system, or just the space left for a text or a lost label. Without inscriptions this cannot be confirmed, so the specific meaning (elements, winds, seasons, tides or a computistical cycle) is uninterpreted.
evidence: Visible: one closed outer circle in yellow; eight paired arcs in yellow, red-brown and green that cross and overlap each other in alternation; a regular, roughly symmetrical arrangement around an empty centre; no legible labels, numbers or names inside the figure. The surrounding text on the page is only partly legible and cannot be used to identify the subject. External: medieval diagrams of the elements, seasons and the cyclical order of the cosmos often use interlocking circles or arcs and colour coding to show reciprocal connection (for example in natural-philosophical and computistical manuscripts), but I cannot name a specific source with confidence.
